title: Tamil Nadu Unveils 'Dream Olympics', Hands Rs 8.25 Crore to Asian Games and Chess Stars
excerpt: CM C. Joseph Vijay's 'Dream Olympics' gives Asian and Commonwealth medallists Rs 50 lakh a year for training plus monthly stipends, as the state doubles down on converting near-misses into Olympic podiums.
body:
• Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay launched the 'Dream Olympics' initiative on October 9 at a Chennai ceremony, presenting Rs 8.25 crore in cash incentives to 18 Tamil Nadu sportspersons.
  • The honorees include medalists and participants from the 20th Asian Games 2026 and the 46th Chess Olympiad 2026, among them G. Kamalini and R. Praggnanandhaa.
  • Dream Olympics gives medallists of the Asian Games, Para Asian Games, and Commonwealth Games Rs 50 lakh per year for training plus a Rs 1 lakh monthly stipend.
  • The state also raised Olympic winner incentives to Rs 5 crore for gold, Rs 3 crore for silver, and Rs 2 crore for bronze — among the richest rewards in the country.

A ceremony at The Leela Palace

Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay launched the 'Dream Olympics' initiative on Thursday at a special felicitation ceremony organized by the Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT) at The Leela Palace in Chennai, honoring athletes from the state who won medals and participated in the 20th Asian Games 2026 and the 46th Chess Olympiad 2026. The government presented Rs 8.25 crore in cash incentives to 18 sportspersons.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Jp8y4LRVOvI

Among the honorees were Madurai-born wicketkeeper-batter G. Kamalini, who won gold with the Indian women's cricket team at the Asian Games, and Grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa, part of the Indian team that won silver at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand.

"CM Vijay said, 'We are there for you.' That's all he said. So I think that is the most important thing any person can say. I think there's no words to explain it. Actually, he's CM, he's Vijay, so there's no words to explain it. It's really a proud moment for me and for my family."

— G. Kamalini, Asian Games cricket gold medallist

Praggnanandhaa, who won bronze on Board 1 at the Olympiad with 6.5/10, thanked the state government for sustained backing: "We won the silver medal in the Chess Olympiad, and it was great that we got to meet the CM and also receive cash in the centre for that. We've been getting great support from the Tamil Nadu government through SDAT. I'm also part of the elite scheme, where I've also been getting support."

What Dream Olympics actually is

The initiative is Tamil Nadu's bid to convert near-misses into Olympic medals. Medallists of the Asian Games, Para Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, and Para Commonwealth Games will receive Rs 50 lakh per year for training, in addition to a Rs 1 lakh monthly stipend. Sports Development Minister Aadhav Arjuna said the chief minister has given the department freedom to create international-level facilities, including an Olympic City and Olympic Centers, with state-of-the-art rehabilitation facilities. SDAT has signed MoUs to upgrade 32 vacant lands as sports grounds, he added.

https://x.com/Olympics/status/2106417316221313040

The government has also increased its Olympic winner incentives to Rs 5 crore for gold, Rs 3 crore for silver, and Rs 2 crore for bronze, with Rs 15 lakh assistance for athletes who qualify for the Olympics.

The chess connection

The felicitation underscored how central chess has become to Tamil Nadu's sporting identity. India finished the 2026 Chess Olympiad with six individual board medals — including silver for D. Gukesh on Open Board 4 and bronze for Praggnanandhaa on Board 1 — plus the Gaprindashvili Cup for the best combined performance in the Open and Women's sections. The open team took silver behind Uzbekistan; the women's team took bronze behind China and Kazakhstan.

At the same ceremony, 12 women players of the Tamil Nadu team that won the National Sub-Junior Women's Basketball Championship received Rs 18 lakh in incentives, and Para Asian Games participants got Rs 7 lakh each as special financial assistance.

Diaspora angle

Tamil Nadu's sports-infrastructure play matters well beyond Chennai. The state has become the nursery for India's chess boom — Gukesh, Praggnanandhaa, and a pipeline of grandmasters all came through its ecosystem — and for the Tamil diaspora in the US, UK, and Singapore, these are hometown heroes. A Rs 50-lakh-a-year training commitment is the kind of structural investment that turns a medal-winning generation into a medal-winning system, and the diaspora watches it closely because it produced the players their children now idolize.

What to watch

The test of Dream Olympics is execution: whether the Olympic City and Olympic Centers materialize, whether the Rs 1 lakh monthly stipends reach athletes without bureaucratic friction, and whether the money translates into podiums at LA 2028. Aadhav Arjuna also proposed making physical training periods mandatory daily in colleges — a cultural nudge that, if implemented, could matter as much as the cash.
